verdicts.quote: All ticket, ID, audit and outbox changes for an import are committed together.
Where applicable include the first offending record number (header is 1), without echoing uploaded values.
verdicts.missing: Only the first offending record is identified. The response has no specified way to report each failed row and its particular reason.

verdicts.quote: Repeating a successful create produces new tickets.
verdicts.missing: This settles a repeat submission. It leaves matching criteria and the treatment of matching rows within a single file unspecified.

verdicts.quote: request to let agents upload a CSV to bulk-create tickets … The existing internal network boundary applies.
verdicts.missing: The specification identifies agents and the network boundary but gives no import-specific permission rule distinguishing importers from callers who can create one ticket.

verdicts.quote: Require one header with title and requester and optional priority, in any order, using those exact names. … Reject empty/header-only input, missing/duplicate/unknown headings
Support comma separation, quoted fields, doubled quotes, LF or CRLF, a UTF-8 BOM, and an optional final record terminator.
verdicts.missing: The example demonstrates an embedded comma. The specification does not say whether a line break inside quotes is retained within the same field.

verdicts.quote: The server validates every row, then stages normal ticket changes. … No ID or notification is consumed by an unsuccessful upload.
Existing MAX_BODY_BYTES applies (65536 by default) … body larger than MAX_BODY_BYTES with HTTP 400 and error.code invalid.
Reject empty/header-only input … Each data record maps to the ordinary ticket fields. … On success return HTTP 201 with a JSON object containing items, in file order.
Repeating a successful create produces new tickets. No upload/session record is held after the response.
The server validates every row, then stages normal ticket changes. T-1 commits those changes and returns 201. The agent can read tickets and audit immediately.
verdicts.missing: HTTP 201 signals completion of the request. There is no background import for large files or completion signal for such a job.

verdicts.quote: Each ticket queues one ticket.created event for its requester. … The existing worker delivers queued notifications asynchronously.
verdicts.missing: The delivery rate and whether a large batch can notify all requesters at once are unspecified.

verdicts.quote: An omitted or empty priority defaults to normal. … Each item is a complete open ticket with its assigned sequential ID.
verdicts.missing: The initial assignee and the timestamps assigned to each ticket are unspecified.

verdicts.quote: CSV is request-scoped and the original file is not retained.
GET /tickets, GET /tickets/:id and the audit read must observe the resulting tickets and the existing actor from X-Actor (or system). … Each audit entry records dana
verdicts.missing: The audit ties created tickets to an actor. It does not specify recording the time of import.

verdicts.where: Behavior model, F-2 and final paragraph
verdicts.quote: The caller can correct and retry. Client disconnect prior to a complete body exits before writes. … Batch progress tracking, cancellation after submission, migrations and expiry add no state.
verdicts.missing: The specification gives no way to cancel during processing. It describes retrying a rejected upload but gives no operation for retrying selected failed rows.

verdicts.quote: No graphical surface or additional throughput/latency SLA was requested. … Batch progress tracking, cancellation after submission, migrations and expiry add no state.
verdicts.missing: There is no completion-time bound for a maximum-size file or specified way for the agent to see progress.

verdicts.quote: Existing ticket reads, JSON creation, transitions, audit, notifications, version 1 data files, CLI and weekly report retain their documented behavior. … Each item is a complete open ticket with its assigned sequential ID.
